title: Three Winters and One Short Rail
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·绘画与艺术）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·绘画与艺术）　|　核心词汇：gallery　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 gallery 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the painter ① opened a gallery that no visitor in the street would have named, and he said the opening was the whole of the winter. The ② gallery, meaning the hall itself and not the painting, ran three winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a gallery, he said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ gallery in that street had the same short rail beside it, and the ④ gallery at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A gallery, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the painter said the naming is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the gallery was the whole of the matter, meaning the balcony and not the hall. The ⑥ gallery, meaning the balcony and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; gallery, he said, is either something you open or the only word that means both a hall and a balcony. He said the balcony is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ gallery had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short rail. The ⑧ gallery of the whole thing, the painter wrote in January, was one street and three winters of naming; gallery, he said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ gallery I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1974 and is still described as the quietest in the street. A ⑩ gallery, my mother said in 1976, is the only one that improves by being named; every gallery, she said, is a balcony that has agreed to look like a hall. She said the balcony was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 画廊；美术馆（指街上每一间旁边的那一间）
B. n. 画廊（指那一间本身，与画作相对）
C. 固定搭配：open a gallery 开设一间画廊
D. n. 画廊（指留给孩子们的那一间）
E. n. 画廊（抽象总称，指一条街上的展陈之事）
F. n. 画廊（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一间）
G. n. （剧场或议会的）楼座；旁听席（指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 楼座（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: opened a gallery that no visitor in the street would have named
The gallery, meaning the hall itself and not the painting
the gallery at the far end
the gallery was the whole of the matter
the gallery had become a line in a plan
The gallery of the whole thing

answers.why: open a gallery 意为“开设一间画廊”，1965 年那位画师开设了一间街上没有一位访客肯说出名字的画廊。
gallery 意为“画廊”，指那一间本身而不是画作，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
gallery 意为“画廊”，指街上每一间旁边的那一间，每一间旁边都有同一道矮矮的栏杆。
gallery 意为“画廊”，指留给孩子们的那一间，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
gallery 意为“楼座、旁听席”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这片楼座就是那件事的全部。
gallery 意为“楼座”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那间画廊，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
gallery 意为“画廊”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一间，到 1972 年这一间成了计划里的一行。
gallery 意为“画廊”，画师一月写道，整件事的展陈之事是一条街道和三个冬天的说出名字。
gallery 意为“画廊”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一间，1974 年结束了，至今仍被说成街上最安静的一间。
gallery 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，一间画廊是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的东西。
